messages:
Hannah Lee: Quick announcement  new vendor onboarding SLA goes live Monday 2026-07-06. Goal: reduce average onboarding time from 12 days to 5 days for low-risk vendors. Details & intake: https://redwood.example.com/finance/vendor-onboarding-sla

Raj Patel: Nice. Whats the definition of a low-risk vendor?

Hannah Lee: Low-risk = vendors that pass standard security questionnaire, have public business registration, and invoices <$25k annually. High-risk (data access, custom integrations) still follow the extended flow.

Procurement Bot: New SLA rules (summary):
```
- Low-risk: onboarding target 5 business days
- Medium-risk: target 10 business days + parallel legal review
- High-risk: custom timeline, security + legal must sign off
- Expedite flag: add `expedite=true` to intake to request faster triage
```

Accounting: For PO creation, we need GL, project_code, and approver email in the intake. Missing fields will cause delay.

Hannah Lee: Agree. We've added a validation step in the Supplier Portal that blocks submission if GL or project_code is empty. That should cut down on back-and-forth.

Security Review: Note: for any vendor that requests data access, include an architecture diagram and data flow CSV in the intake. We'll auto-assign the security reviewer based on the vendor type.

Raj Patel: If a team wants to fast-track a vendor demo that's time-sensitive, how do we request a provisional vcard?

Hannah Lee: Use the `virtual-card` workflow and set `purpose=demo` and `expires_at` to the demo end date. Procurement can approve vcards for sandbox/demo only; sandbox data access still requires security signoff.

Procurement Bot: Automated: onboarding SLA dashboard published to Console -> Procurement -> KPIs. Teams: react with :white_check_mark: once you've read.

Raj Patel: Reacted. :white_check_mark:

Hannah Lee: Thanks all. We'll run a 20-min Q&A on Friday 9am PT to walk through the portal changes and the new intake fields. Invite will go out shortly. Ping #procurement-help for one-off cases.
